meaning: a small visible part of a much larger problem or situation
literal_translation: лише невелика видима частина значно більшої проблеми
example: The 2% drop in sales is just the tip of the iceberg.
origin: Refers to the fact that most of an iceberg lies hidden under the water, so only its top is visible.

wrong_meanings.meaning: the highest point of a trend line
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to a small visible part of a hidden whole, not to the peak of a trend on a graph.
The idiom describes a small part of a larger problem, not a surprising achievement.

wrong_meanings.meaning: a warning that the weather will get colder
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has no link to weather or temperature; it is about the hidden size of a problem.

explanation: 'The tip of the iceberg' describes a small visible part of a problem that is much larger than it appears. Most of an iceberg is hidden under the water, just as most of a problem may be hidden from view.
